strategy.summary: Reproduce SymPy numerical blow-up in Matrix.inv() and Matrix.exp() for symbolic polynomial/rational-function matrices that embed Float coefficients, using the project’s own regression tests from sympy/matrices/tests/test_matrixbase.py added in/around PR #26833. The transition is: the buggy revision fails the new assertions that bound the maximum magnitude of Float atoms in the result (<1e3), while the fixed revision passes.

build_commands: python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
pinned_because: SymPy must be tested specifically on the buggy commit c1b1d2d70164 and then on the post-PR fixed revision (the one that contains the changes from PR #26833 and makes these assertions pass).

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (git checkout c1b1d2d70164), the test(s) fail because max(abs(f) for f in Mi.atoms(Float)) (and/or for Me.atoms(Float)) exceeds 1e3 due to unnecessarily large Float atoms (reported up to ~1.14555615673900e+251 in the issue). On the fixed revision (the revision that includes PR #26833 changes), the same assertions pass because Matrix.inv()/Matrix.exp() uses exact rational coefficients internally for matrices of polynomials or rational functions when the matrix has symbolic expressions with float coefficients, preventing the appearance of such huge Float atoms.
strategy.numerical_probe: The tests compute max(abs(f) for f in Mi.atoms(Float)) and max(abs(f) for f in Me.atoms(Float)) and assert it is < 1e3. (No other numeric inspection is used for pass/fail.)

input_output_examples.input: Me = M.exp() where M is the 7x7 Matrix from issue #26821 built using float literals (1.0 etc.) in the entries, then Me.atoms(Float) is computed
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Float atoms include magnitudes as large as 1.14555615673900e+251 (also e.g. 5.72778078369499e+250, 1.53090103458042e+200).
input_output_examples.expected_output: No unnecessarily large floating point coefficients; the result’s Float atoms should be bounded below 1e3 in magnitude per the regression test.

input_output_examples.input: Mi = M.inv(); simplify(M*Mi) is checked for identity; then Mi.atoms(Float) is computed
input_output_examples.buggy_output: simplify(M*Mi) yields the correct identity, but Mi.atoms(Float) includes extremely large floats such as -1.145556156739e+251 and -5.72778078369499e+250 (and corresponding large positive values), so the max(abs(f)) bound is violated.
input_output_examples.expected_output: The identity property remains; additionally, Mi.atoms(Float) should not contain unnecessarily large magnitudes, so max(abs(f)) < 1e3.

risks: This is likely sensitive to SymPy version/patch level: the environment must run the exact buggy commit c1b1d2d70164 and then the fixed revision that includes PR #26833. Using an older/newer release that already includes the fix will prevent the buggy test failure transition.

The exponential test is marked @slow; ensure pytest configuration does not skip slow tests (default pytest runs them; but some CI configs may use --skip-slow). If it is skipped, only the inverse test can be used to verify the transition.

The failure mode is magnitude-driven; the test threshold (<1e3) is the oracle. If a particular build/platform changes Float representation/scaling enough to keep max(abs(f)) under 1e3, the failure may not reproduce, but the upstream issue reports values up to ~1e251, so this is expected to be stable across typical platforms.

No documented toolchain constraints are provided in the evidence; if SymPy is built/compiled with unusual flags (not typical for SymPy’s pure-Python core), reproduction should still be attempted under a standard CPython environment.

oracle.reference_source: The project regression tests in sympy/matrices/tests/test_matrixbase.py added for issue/PR #26821/#26833.
oracle.why: Success/failure is determined solely by the assertion: max(abs(f) for f in Mi.atoms(Float)) < 1e3 and similarly for Me. This is an exact inequality check on the computed Float atoms, not on a separately validated numeric result.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion sees at least one Float atom in Mi.atoms(Float) (and/or Me.atoms(Float)) with magnitude >> 1e3 (issue reports ~1e200 to ~1e251), so max(abs(f)) >= 1e3 and the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After applying PR #26833’s change (Matrix.inv() uses exact rational coefficients internally for matrices of polynomials/rational functions when the matrix has symbolic expressions with float coefficients, and the corresponding exponential behavior is corrected as well), the Float atoms in the result are no longer explosively large, so max(abs(f)) < 1e3 and the tests pass.
